note: Every public claim, with its evidence and the test that keeps it honest. Status: established (evidence recorded and tested), documented_limitation (a recorded failure the docs must keep stating), under_validation (pre-registered, runs in progress), not_established (not claimed). tests/test_claims.py fails if recorded evidence stops supporting an established claim or a limitation.

claims.statement: The primary verdict is PASS exactly when the lower bound of the 95% interval for the held-out gain exceeds the declared minimum gain, FAIL when the upper bound is below it, INCONCLUSIVE otherwise; the conditional-information test drives no verdict or gate
Items sharing a group never sit in both the training and the test fold
The verdict does not change under monotone rescaling of the score
The secondary conditional-information test keeps its false-flag rate at or below 0.10 on the 13 registered no-signal scenarios of the 0.7 suite (it does not on the structures in CLAIM-019)
--fast detects moderate and strong planted signal in at least 80% of runs
On real detectors the tool reproduces seven independent prior analyses (verdict, magnitude within the prior interval widened by 0.02, ordering)
On real data structures with the detector replaced by a no-information one, every false-flag rate is at most 0.10
Editing any file in an evidence package, or removing or reordering a ledger entry, is detected by verify-evidence
The package opens no network connection
The binary engine's output is fixed to 1e-12 for a given version and pinned dependencies
A policy cannot invoke an uncalibrated rule (minimum gain, other alpha, other metric)
A super-learner null keeps interaction-only detectors at or below 0.10 false flags

The increment's 95% clustered DeLong interval covers the mean estimate at 0.905-0.965 in six registered scenarios (target 0.85-0.99); descriptive, not used for the decision; not validated for detectors that are exact functions of the baselines
The omitted-baseline sensitivity analysis gives no false comfort against simulated omitted baselines (V1: gain survives in 98.0% pooled, >= 93.8% per family, when the erasure index is <= 0.5)

The sample-size planner's power predictions hold under its own and a misspecified generator (0.13 planner targeted the experimental permutation test; stopped, see PREREG_0.13 addendum 3; re-registered for the PASS verdict in PREREG_PLAN2)
A minimum-gain acceptance gate
Increments generalise across datasets or models (formal heterogeneity test)
Construct validity: that the label measures what the evaluator is claimed to measure

The conditional-information test is unreliable when a baseline's effect differs by category, or the score is an XOR-like or three-way function of the baselines; on real TREC data a no-information judge was flagged 33% of the time and within-query stratification did not fix it (29%)

A positive gain can be a model-class gain: when the score encodes a function of the baselines the baseline models do not learn at the sample size, the gain shrinks as data grow (three-way: +0.115 at 600 items, +0.053 at 3,000)

Across 32 pre-registered structures (R1: diagnostic D1-D10, controls N0/P1/P2 at 600 and 3,000 items, uneven groups, clustered noise, rare positives, few groups), the 95% interval for the gain covered the expected gain in 0.87-0.98 of 200 runs in 30 structures; every no-signal and signal control passed at both sizes

The default interval is not validated when the score is a three-way interaction of baselines and a category (R1 structure D4): coverage 0.845 at 600 items and 0.695 at 3,000. A refit-aware interval (--interval refit) covers 0.985 at both sizes but is conservative under the null (1.000); it ships as opt-in (PREREG_R1b.md §7, outcome 2).
